Arrays_and_Hashing.title: Arrays & Hashing
Arrays_and_Hashing.summary: Trade memory for time: a hash map or set answers "have I seen this / how many times?" in O(1), turning nested loops into one pass. Cue: pairs, duplicates, anagrams, frequencies, grouping.

Two_Pointers.title: Two Pointers
Two_Pointers.summary: Two indices that move toward each other or at different speeds over a sorted array, a string or a linked list. Cue: sorted input, pairs or triplets with a target sum, in-place compaction, palindromes, cycle detection.

Sliding_Window.title: Sliding Window
Sliding_Window.summary: Grow the right edge, shrink the left edge while the window breaks a rule, and update the answer as you go: O(n) for contiguous subarrays and substrings. Cue: "longest/shortest/count of contiguous …" with a constraint.

Binary_Search.title: Binary Search
Binary_Search.summary: Halve a sorted space each step, either an array or the range of possible answers. Cue: sorted or rotated input, "minimum X such that …", a monotonic yes/no check, n up to 10⁹.

Prefix_Sum.title: Prefix Sum & Difference Arrays
Prefix_Sum.summary: Precompute running totals so any range sum is one subtraction; difference arrays do the reverse for range updates. Cue: many range-sum queries, "subarray sum equals k" (prefix sum + hash map).

Stack.title: Stack & Monotonic Stack
Stack.summary: Last-in-first-out for matching and nesting; a monotonic stack finds the next greater or smaller element for every index in O(n). Cue: parentheses, expression parsing, "next greater", histogram areas.

Linked_List.title: Linked List
Linked_List.summary: Pointer surgery with a dummy head, reversal in place, and fast/slow pointers for the middle or a cycle. Cue: "reverse", "merge", "reorder", "detect a cycle", O(1) extra space.

Trees.title: Trees & BST
Trees.summary: Recursion on left and right subtrees (DFS) or level by level (BFS); BST order gives sorted traversal and O(h) search. Cue: depth, paths, ancestors, level views, validating or building trees.

Trie.title: Trie
Trie.summary: A tree of characters for prefix queries over many words. Cue: autocomplete, "starts with", word search on a board, maximum XOR (binary trie).

Top_K_Elements.title: Heap / Top-K
Top_K_Elements.summary: A heap of size k keeps the best k items in O(n log k); quickselect or bucket sort can beat sorting. Cue: "k largest/smallest/most frequent", merging k sorted lists, a running median (two heaps).

Intervals.title: Intervals
Intervals.summary: Sort by start (or end), then merge, count overlaps or sweep through events. Cue: meetings, ranges, overlapping segments, "minimum rooms", inserting into a sorted range list.

Greedy.title: Greedy
Greedy.summary: Take the locally best choice when an exchange argument shows it never hurts. Cue: scheduling, jumps, gas stations, "minimum number of …" where sorting reveals the order to decide in.

Backtracking.title: Backtracking
Backtracking.summary: Build candidates one choice at a time and undo the choice on the way back, pruning dead branches early. Cue: "all subsets / permutations / combinations", constraint puzzles, n up to about 15-20.

Graphs.title: Graphs: BFS, DFS & Topological Sort
Graphs.summary: Explore nodes with BFS (shortest path in unweighted graphs) or DFS (components, cycles), on explicit edges or a grid; topological sort orders dependencies. Cue: islands, flood fill, prerequisites, word ladders.

Graph_Shortest_Path.title: Shortest Paths
Graph_Shortest_Path.summary: Dijkstra for non-negative weights, 0-1 BFS for weights of 0 or 1, Bellman-Ford with negative edges or a hop limit, Floyd-Warshall for all pairs on small graphs. Cue: "cheapest / fastest route".

Graph_Advanced.title: Union-Find, MST & Advanced Graphs
Graph_Advanced.summary: Union-Find for dynamic connectivity, Kruskal or Prim for minimum spanning trees, Tarjan for bridges and articulation points, Eulerian paths. Cue: "connect everything cheaply", "critical connection", merging groups.

DP.title: Dynamic Programming (1-D & General)
DP.summary: Define a state, write the recurrence from smaller states, then fill a table bottom-up or memoize top-down. Cue: "number of ways", "min/max cost", choices at each step with overlapping subproblems.

DP_Knapsack.title: DP: Knapsack
DP_Knapsack.summary: Pick items under a capacity: 0/1 (each item once, iterate capacity downward) or unbounded (reuse items, iterate upward). Cue: subset sums, partitions, coin change, "target sum".

DP_Grid_and_Strings.title: DP: Grids, Strings & State Machines
DP_Grid_and_Strings.summary: Two-dimensional states: dp[i][j] over a grid or over prefixes of two strings, plus state machines such as buy/sell/cooldown. Cue: edit distance, LCS, unique paths, stock problems with limits.

DP_Advanced.title: DP: Interval, Bitmask, Digit, Tree & Matrix Power
DP_Advanced.summary: DP over intervals (burst balloons), bitmasks (visit all nodes), digits (count numbers ≤ N), trees (rerooting) and matrix powers (linear recurrences with huge n). Cue: n ≤ 20 for bitmasks, "count integers in [L, R]".

Bit_Manipulation.title: Bit Manipulation
Bit_Manipulation.summary: Work on the bits directly: XOR cancels pairs, `x & (x - 1)` drops the lowest set bit, masks enumerate subsets. Cue: "single number", powers of two, counting bits, no extra space.

Math.title: Math, Number Theory, Geometry & Games
Math.summary: Number theory (gcd, sieve, modular inverse), combinatorics (nCr mod p), geometry, and game theory (Grundy numbers). Cue: answers "modulo 10⁹ + 7", divisibility, primes, "both players play optimally".

Range_Queries.title: Range Queries: Segment & Fenwick Trees
Range_Queries.summary: Segment trees and Fenwick trees answer range queries and point (or range) updates in O(log n). Cue: many interleaved updates and range sum/min/max queries, counting inversions or smaller elements.

Strings.title: Strings & String Matching
Strings.summary: Parsing and comparing strings, plus linear-time matching: KMP and the Z-function, rolling hashes, Manacher for palindromes. Cue: find a pattern, repeated substrings, longest palindrome, string rotations.

Design.title: Design
Design.summary: Build a class whose operations meet stated complexity targets by combining structures (hash map + linked list for LRU, two stacks for a queue). Cue: "design / implement" with O(1) operations.

Divide_and_Conquer.title: Divide & Conquer, Meet in the Middle
Divide_and_Conquer.summary: Split into halves, solve each recursively, combine; meet in the middle enumerates each half of a search space and joins them. Cue: merge sort, building trees from traversals, fast power, n ≈ 40 subset problems.

Matrix_and_Simulation.title: Matrix & Simulation
Matrix_and_Simulation.summary: Carefully implement a process exactly as described: spirals, rotations, in-place markers, text layout, numeral conversions. Cue: no clever algorithm needed, just index bookkeeping without off-by-one errors.
